properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 11/08/2021 to INFLECTION ENERGY (PA) LLC in Eldred Twp, Lycoming county. 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: INFLECTION ENERGY (PA) LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 11/08/2021
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 935828
Permit API: 081-21461
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Eldred Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 11/08/2021
Comments: On November 8, 2021, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a site inspection for a reported spill at the Inflection Energy TLC Pad. The DEP received a phone call from Inflection Energy Zac Subra on November 6, 2021 about a release of production fluid during a pressure test. The DEP met with Inflection Energy Joe Zoka. During a pressure test for the preparation of flowback of the recently drilled wells, a valve was left open. The open valve spilled about 28 gallons of brine fluid to the pad surface. The impacted area was excavated immediately. Inflection scraped about 3 inches of a 15 ft. by 10 ft. area. The impacted soil was then loaded into a covered container to be hauled to the landfill. The containment around the flowback equipment appears to be in good condition. Inflection is planning to begin flowback process on Tuesday. Violations of the Clean Streams Law 402(b), ¿78a.56(a), and SWMA 301 are noted but have been immediately corrected. Outstanding violations remain from Inspection Report 3257683.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: NUCOMER ENERGY LLC
Violation Type: Administrative
Violation Date: 8/03/2021

Violation ID: 925128
Permit API: 085-24339
Unconventional: No
County: Mercer
Municipality: West Salem Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/03/2021
Comments: Field inspection performed in afternoon with warm, sunny weather conditions and 68 degrees. Last inspection performed on 2/4/19, over 2 years ago. Wellhead located in agriculture field planted with corn ~1300' WSW of surface equipment. At the wellhead vegetation is extremely overgrown, both lower production tubular valves at head are closed, and the production tubular plumbed to sales/surface equipment valve is open; annulus is buried below grade, could not determine if vented; pump jack present with motor at wellhead overgrown with vegetation (photos #1, #2, and #3). No Well label/marker affixed to wellhead. Some fair to moderate corrosion at the wellhead on the production/surface casing steel unions, lubricator, and tubulars. Notice of violation (NOV) issued for well labeling OGA3211(H). The surface/ground production equipment, one 50 bbl poly tank and one 150 bbl steel tank contained by earthen dike (photo #4). Well posting signage affixed to steel tank, but operator details need added (i.e. address) (photo #9). Valves are closed at production equipment to separator and no production chart is present (photo #5). Plumbed meter line with house gas meter run on opposite tubular from separator with open valve (photo #6). Meter reading (photo #7). Staining with petro odor present on ground out front of plumbed meter line drip valve. The area of staining appears sprayed from drip valve covering an area of approximately 20'x6' (photo #8). Fair to moderate corrosion on ground production unit. Operator contact information needs added to posting (i.e. address). Request Operator address information be added to posting. Operator has not submitted 2020 Mechanical Integrity Assessment (MIA) for this well. Notice of violation (NOV) issued for MIA Reporting 78.88(e). Operator has submitted annual production report (APR) for 2020 for this well stating 224 MCF recorded over 182 days. This is an active, producing well.

properties.summary: Administrative violation issued on 12/09/2022 to NUCOMER ENERGY LLC in West Salem Twp, Mercer county. OGA3211(G) - WELL PERMITS - POSTING - Failure to post the well permit number and the operator's name, address and phone number at the well site during construction of the access road, site preparation and during drilling, operating or alteration of well.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: NUCOMER ENERGY LLC
Violation Type: Administrative
Violation Date: 12/09/2022
Violation Code: OGA3211(G) - WELL PERMITS - POSTING - Failure to post the well permit number and the operator's name, address and phone number at the well site during construction of the access road, site preparation and during drilling, operating or alteration of well.
Violation ID: 977985
Permit API: 085-24169
Unconventional: No
County: Mercer
Municipality: West Salem Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 12/09/2022
Comments: Routine field inspection performed in late morning with cold, partly sunny weather conditions, and 40 degrees. Last inspection performed on 8/6/18, more than 4 years ago. Wellhead is located in soybean Agriculture field planted/harvested ~350' NNW of surface/ground production equipment (photo #1). The wellhead is in close, visible proximity to the production facility (photo #2). At the wellhead surface casing valve is open, lower right side production tubular valve cracked open to port with valve open to drip/domestic house gas meter run, lower production tubular right side valve is closed, upper production tubular is plumbed with t-shaped tubular and closed valve union, and the production tubular plumbed on left side (opposite meter) of head to sales/surface equipment with open valve; annulus is exposed and vented to the atmosphere with plumbed tubular sticking out of ground and open valve union (photos #3, #4, and #5). Meter reading (photo #6). No Well label/marker is affixed to wellhead. The wellhead is in close, visible proximity to the production facility and does not require a well label/marker. Some trace to occasionally moderate corrosion at the wellhead on the production/surface casing steel unions, lubricator, and tubulars. The surface/ground production facility, one 50 bbl poly tank, and one 100 bbl steel tank all contained by a shallow earthen dike (photo #5). Functioning pressure gauge atop separator unit in line recording ~40 psi at time of inspection (photo #6). Valve open on main tubular feeding separator and open valves to and from separator (photo #7). A 31-day production chart is present with recordings and dated 12/1/22 (photo #8). Well posting signage affixed to steel tank with all information about well and current Operator present, except the Operator contact address information (photo #9). Fair to occasionally moderate corrosion on ground production unit equipment and tank. Notice of violation (NOV) issued for Well posting OGA3211(G). The Department is requesting Operator add contact address information to the permanent well posting signage affixed at the surface production facility. The Operator has not submitted 2021 Mechanical Integrity Assessment (MIA) for this well. No MIA submitted by the Operator for 2021, 2020, and 2019. The last MIA value officially submitted was back in 2018 stating 55 psig. Notice of violation (NOV) issued for Operating Wells - Mechanical Integrity reporting 78.88(e). The Operator submitted annual production reported (APR) in 2021 of 0 Mcf recorded over 365 days. The 2021 annual production report submitted indicates that this well was not in production during the 2021 production year. Additionally, this well was noted as having 0 or blank production values under the gas and/or oil quantity columns and noted as Well Temporarily Not Producing under the non production comments columns of the 2021 and 2020 production reports. The last reported production value was in 2019 of 3,627 Mcf recorded over 365 days. Wellhead field verified and GPS coordinates of well updated with this inspection showed a minimal distance offset of ~22 ft between coordinates (photo #10). This well appears to be back in production based on this inspection, the chart at facility with recordings, and the open valves with meter at wellhead. This is an active, producing well with a domestic house gas meter at wellhead.

Inspection Date: 2020-01-23
Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a FUI of the Marshlands Play, Pierson 801 Well Pad located in Gaines Twp, Tioga Co. on 1/23/2020 @1142 hours. The weather was 22 degrees, partly cloudy, humidity 55%, winds SSW 8 mph. No activity or personnel was observed onsite. The trench and excavated area, related to the previous release behind the GPU's, appears to still be open and is temporarily covered by black material. It does not appear any backfilling has taken place. No fluid or staining was observed on the pad surface. The fluid in the secondary containment surrounding the production tanks appeared frozen. A small duck pond was observed holding "annulus fluid" and "used oil" totes. The staining on the totes appears to indicate they are almost at capacity. These should be removed for proper disposal. A duck pond does not appear to have adequate storage to accommodate the total volume of fluid in the totes. Violations cited 9/30/2019 in IR#2939891, remain OUTSTANDING against API#117-20309 from a previous release. Site remediation is ongoing. Once a Remediation Action Completion Report has been submitted to DEP's Environmental Cleanups and Brownfields program for review, and attainment with Act 2 standards has be confirmed, the outstanding violations will be closed. No new violations are noted at this time. I departed the site at 1215 hours.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2019-09-09 to Swn Prod Co Llc in Stevens Twp, Bradford county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Swn Prod Co Llc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2019-09-09
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 862178
Permit API: 015-20889
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Stevens Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-09-09
Comments: On 09/07/19 at 1130 hrs, Steve Moyer notified Phone Duty Officer (Andrew Hobbins)reporting that two puddles on the GU-J-Pad well pad surface tested high for conductivity while removing containment. The first puddle measured approximately 11mS/cm and the other puddle measured 3-4 mS/cm. Mr. Moyer reported that containment cleanup was ongoing, but currently the impacted pad surface is limited to a 30 foot by 40 foot area near the well heads, and a second area is still being investigated is ranging up to 7 mS/cm conductivity and is roughly 50 feet by 60 feet.  Mr. Moyer attributed the high conductivity to a hole somewhere in the containment liner, but no holes were found. A vac truck removed the puddles from the pad surface. Resource Environmental was contracted to delineate the impacted area and do remediation work. SWN finished their drill out and was currently setting up to hook up flow lines for the new wells. No waterways or stormwater/infiltration areas were affected. On September 09, 2019 Department representative Jared Jacobini (Water Quality Specialist) conducted a site inspection in response to an incident reported on 09/07/19 by Steve Moyer (Southwestern Energy (SWN) Regulatory Supervisor) at SWNs WELL PAD J. Also present for the inspection was production supervisor Mike Deming of SWN. When I arrived onsite, the operator had scraped excavated impacted soils near the well cellars and towards the low area on the pad near the level spreader (Photo # 1-8). The excavated soil had been removed and placed into seven roll offs and was being removed during the inspection. At the time of inspection, the volume and cause of the release was not know but was still being investigated with anticipation of pursuing Act 2. The pad surface was screened with a soil probe conductivity meter and a handheld conductivity meter throughout the impacted and excavated area, puddles, and outside of the pad below the level spreader. In one location that did not appear to have been excavated, the soil conductivity was 3.43 mS/ cm (Photo # 9-10). In a second location beyond the well heads along the western pad border a puddle exhibiting a sheen had a conductivity of 1,126 µS/cm (Photo # 12). Mike Deming said that he would have the area were soil conductivity was high scraped up and the location of puddled water vacuumed up. This release should be remediated in accordance with Chapter 78a66(c). As a result of the presence of a pollutional substance discovered on the pad surface the following violations are being cited.

Report Details

Permit API: 129-26521
Unconventional: No

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 7/22/2025
Comments: On July 22, 2025, an inspection was conducted at the Chabal 2 well site in Upper Burrell Township, Westmoreland County. The purpose of this inspection was to follow up to IR 3985188 where violations issued from IR 3965337 were left outstanding. During the time of IR 3985188, remedial excavation was completed and the impacted soil was stockpiled onsite awaiting disposal. The impacted soil stockpiles were covered and appeared to be adequately protected to mitigate risk of the impact being spread by stormwater.The following was observed:The well head is equipped with a well tag and appears to be free of fluid leaks at the time of inspection (see photo 2). However, leaking gas was audible from the top of the well head (see photo 3). The operator's information is posted on the separator (see photo 4). The brine tank that was present at the time of the Department's previous surface inspection has been replaced. The newly-installed brine tank appears to be sound at the time of inspection, with no elevated soil conductivity detected underneath the brine tank valve (see photos 7-9 and 18). It appears that the stained material noted underneath the brine tank during the time of IR 3967072 has been removed (see photo 10). It appears that the impacted soil stockpiles have been removed from site, as they were not present onsite during this inspection.The slope that was impacted by the 4/24/2025 release has been backfilled, mulched, and seeded. It has established some vegetative coverage, although it is inconsistent at the time of inspection (see photos 11, 13, and 14). An erosion rill has developed at the top of this slope (see photo 12). Compost Filter Sock (CFS) and straw bales are installed at the bottom of the formerly impacted slope (see photo 15). No elevated soil conductivity was detected in this location or at the approximate downslope edge of the formerly impacted area (see photos 16-18).The Department notified the operator of the erosion rill observed during this inspection via voicemail, and recommended that it is repaired and measures are taken to protect it from heavy stormwater events while it establishes vegetative coverage.Based on observations from this inspection, it appears that remedial work has been completed and the site awaits completion of re-stabilization. However, violations issued from IR 3965337 shall remain outstanding, as an NOI to Remediate and/or Final Report has not yet been submitted to the Department's ECB for review.Additional violations may be forthcoming pending reassessment and reevaluation of the erosion rill in a future follow-up inspection conducted by the Department.

Comments: On 07/24/2024 the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a routine inspection of Southwestern's (SWN's) Vanorder-Patrick (12 Pad) Well Pad in Herrick Township, Bradford County. The weather was 70 degrees and cloudy. Rain fell on the pad within the last24 hours. I arrived at 1035 hours. The site remains stabilized with greater than 70% perennial vegetative cover. Pooled water on the pad was field measured for Electrical Conductivity (EC) between 192.8-262 us/cm. There was no evidence of any spills or releases. There were numerous temporary storage tanks held within secondary containment onsite. Violations remain outstanding at this site from a previous release. Site remediation has been performed and a Remediation Action Completion Report has been submitted to DEPs Environmental Cleanups and Brownfields program for review. The outstanding violations will be closed once attainment with Act 2 standards has be confirmed.The DEP recommends:1. Disposing of stormwater held in the secondary containment structures as soon as possible to maintain compliance with 25 PA 78a64a(e).I departed at 1135 hours.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: GREYLOCK PROD LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 12/09/2024
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8210426
Permit API: 105-21962
Unconventional: Yes
County: Potter
Municipality: Hector Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 12/09/2024
Comments: On 12/09/2024 a representative from the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow-up inspection of Greylock Production LLC's Ron multi-well pad located in Hector Township, Potter County. Upon arrival to the site at 1200 hours, weather was 40F and raining. An Act 9 sign and well permits are visible and located at the site entrance (photo #1).Stimulation activities for the two recently drilled wells are ongoing, equipment is located onsite to support these activities (photos #2-5). See inspection report #3878285 for more details. The accessible area excavated due to the release noted in inspection report #3878285 has been backfilled and fluids in this area field measured for electrical conductivity (EC) at a range of ~701-741us/cm (photo #6). The remaining impacted area from this release will be excavated and backfilled upon removal of the rig matting covering that area. DEP Environmental Cleanups and Brownsfield personnel were onsite prior to my arrival to follow up on the release detailed in inspection report #3878285 and noted concerns regarding a diesel sheen observed on portions of the pad surface.The source of the diesel was investigated by Greylock and it was determined that a maintenance truck located onsite had released an undetermined amount of diesel, the truck was removed from the site and staff were working on removing diesel from the pad surface at the time of this inspection (photos #7-10). Fluid was observed overtopping from the secondary containment structure of the produced fluids offload area onsite (photos #11 and 12). This fluid was combining with rainwater and the diesel sheen on the pad surface and moving into the pad's drainage system which transports water from the pad surface to the site's post-construction stormwater management (PCSM) control. Fluids on the pad surface near the offload containment structure field measured for EC at ~10.32-15.93mS/cm; personnel from Penn E and R measured a similar result of 11.10mS/cm (photos #14-16).The pad drainage system services the site's infiltration basin via two pipes which move fluids from their respective half of the pad (photo #17). One pipe is located closer to the produced fluids offload area and the other is located near the wellheads. Fluid with a diesel sheen was observed discharging into the infiltration basin from the pipe near the offload area; this fluid field measured for EC at ~1.35mS/cm and the soil near this area field measured for EC at ~1.20mS/cm (photos #18-20). Fluid discharging from the pipe near the wellheads field measured for EC at ~0.908mS/cm (photo #21). Vacuum trucks were dispatched to remove fluids from the secondary containment structures and the pad surface in response to the release (photo #22). Personnel were also working to install sump pumps and shut in the drainage pipes to prevent any further discharge into the basin.I followed up with Greylock and they informed me that the drains discharging into the basin were shut in at 1400 hours and they were recovering fluids from basin with a vacuum truck.The DEP recommends the following:-Continuing to prevent fluids from reaching PCSM controls until all contaminated fluids and soils are recovered.-Removing fluids from containment structures as it accumulates.-Following Act 2 to remediate the infiltration basin, diesel spill, and produced fluids containment release.Based on the results of this inspection, the following violations are cited against API #105-21962:-25 PA 78a64a(f) due to the observation of produced fluids overtopping from a secondary containment structure and being conveyed into the sites PCSM controls. -35 P.S. 691.401 due to the release of produced fluids and diesel discharging into the site's PCSM controls.The violations cited in inspection report #3878285 remain outstanding due to the remediation requirements outlined in 25 PA 78a.66(c)(2)(i) having not yet been met.I departed the site at 1345.

Comments: Routine site inspection on December 10, 2024. No E and S issues were observed. Flakey paint and corrosion was observed on the production equipment and axillary pipes. The Department recommends monitoring the equipment and repainting or replacing the equipment if needed. The brine tank is roughly 1/8 of the way full of fluids. A 5x Altair gas meter was used to screen around the production equipment. No combustible or methane gases were detected. Please note a drip was observed coming from the release valve on the poly brine. I screened the area using a Hanna soil probe, the highest reading was >4.00 mS/cm. The impacted area based off soil screenings is approximately the size of basketball in diameter. I collected a soil sample 3442-792 and sent it to the Departments lab in Harrisburg to be analyzed for SAC 530 plus bromide, lithium, and strontium. The operator (Dan Sinclair) was notified via phone on December 11, 2024 at approximately 0900 of the brine leak.Violations have been cited.

Comments: On December 26, 2019; I conducted a site inspection of the Jodikinos Carol 11380 2 H well. The inspection in response to a one barrel reuse water spill reported on 12/24/2019. The following was reported " On 12/24/2019 at 8:30 AM, during a site inspection conducted by Range Environmental Compliance it was discovered that approximately one barrel of reuse water was released to the graveled well pad. After further investigation it was discovered that a seam in the secondary containment had parted which allowed the fluid to release to the graveled well pad. An onsite vacuum truck was utilized to recover standing fluid and Specialized Professional Services Inc. (SPSI) responded to the location for remedial activities. Range intends to remediate this release in accordance with §78a.66(c)(2)." At the time of inspection, the Operator was actively stimulating the 3H well. I observed three sumps installed in the well pad along the south side of the well pad. The sumps appeared to be perforated five-gallon bucks buried in the well pad and equipped with a submersible pump. Comments: On 03/11/2024, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Molek F19 well site following violations issued on 12/08/2023 (IR 3657799, Enforcement 419234). I was accompanied by Environmental Trainees Olivia Holley, Madison Raviart, and Christina Mauri (PA DEP).On 12/08/2023, violations of 102.11(a), 102.22(a)2ii, and 78.53 were issued as outstanding for the access road. Inspection from 12/28/2023 noted that the violations were still open, however the operator was in compliance with schedule. On 01/24/2024, the violations were outstanding (IR 3701625). The following was observed:Some stabilization was used along the upper portion of the access road. Several areas throughout the entire access road did not have stabilization on the open soils. I recommend that stabilization is applied (Photos 1-4). Some areas had vegetation establishing (Photos 2, 4, 5).The channel that runs along the access road did not have rip rap or stabilization. Accelerated erosion and sediment accumulation were noted within this channel, which leads to several culverts along the road (Photo 6).The upper culvert, located at 40.113707 -79.966213, had sediment accumulation within the collection point. I recommend that this is addressed (Photo 7). The culvert located at 40.11300, -79.96751 had large amounts of sediment accumulated within the collection point. The culvert was not able to be seen due to the large amount of sediment within this area (Photos 8, 9). Accelerated erosion was noted within the accumulated sediment (Photo 9). The outlet point of this culvert was covered by the roads gravel/dirt, which was causing accelerated erosion and sediment transport towards the vegetation (Photos 10-12). I recommend that this is addressed. The culvert leading to the collection box was not functioning. Sediment was accumulated and an entry point into the pipe was approximately 99% covered. Accelerated erosion and sedimentation throughout the area and vegetation were noted leading from the channel towards the collection box. There was some sediment laden water within this box. This outlets into the vegetation, where sediment accumulation was noted. The vegetation was accumulating water, which leads towards the stream within the wood line (Photos 13-19). The lower culvert outlets into a channel. Sediment accumulation was noted within the channel. I recommend that rip rap is used within this channel, as this leads directly to the stream (Photos 20, 21).The culverts along the first portion of the access road, near the site gate, were not cleaned out. Potholes along the road were not addressed. Channelization was noted leading from the potholes off of the road. The beginning of the access road, where it meets the township road, was not addressed. This area was previously displaying high levels of flow, leading onto the township road, and depositing sediment. This was noted within IR 3701625, photos 24 and 15 (Photos 22-25). The violations issued on 01/24/2024, IR 3701625, remain outstanding.

Comments: On December 13, 2022, DEP representatives Brad Kline, John Ciccone, and Amber Boyd conducted a routine site inspection at the STL Resources Sturgis South Pad. At the time of inspection, the recently stimulated wells were in flow back. This inspection is to follow up with the multiple spills at this site. About half of the containment from the recent stimulation process has been removed. With the removal of some of the containment STL was able to excavate the area of elevated conductivity off the east end of the containment found on October 24, 2022. The area of excavation was about 90 ft. x 45 ft. and about 8 to 12 inches deep. The second area of elevated conductivity has been excavated to the containment. Containment remains in this area for the flow back process. Seth Rodriguez with STL Resources was onsite and said STL Resources plans to continue the investigation of the extent of this spill area once the containment has been removed. The top layer of soil has been removed in this area adjacent to the containment in about a 10 ft. x 10 ft. area. Soil conductivity could not be screened in either of the excavated areas due to the ground being frozen.The inspection is also to follow up with a spill of production fluid of an estimated 1,600 barrels, when a hose broke on a frac tank. The production fluid overflowed the containment of the frac tanks and spilled on to the pad surface and flowed off of thewell pad on January 8, 2022. STL Resources is continuing to monitor and vacuum the water that is accumulating in the northwest and southwest stormwater vaults. This water is being hauled off site or pumped into frac tanks onsite. The water was not at a level where it could be screened for conductivity with the field meter in the northwest stormwater vault. In the southwest stormwater vault, the conductivity of the water was 1,939 uS/cm. The DEP screened the five seeps and four stream sampling sites for conductivity with a field water quality meter. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 1 (4) had conductivity of 21.2 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 2 (3) had conductivity of 21.3 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 3 (2) had a conductivity of 23.7 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 4 (1) had a conductivity of 23.8 uS/cm. Seep 1 had a conductivity of 71.9 uS/cm. Seep 1a had a conductivity of 133.7 uS/cm. Seep 2 had a conductivity of 32 uS/cm. Seep 3 was not able to be screened with the conductivity meter due to the lack of water at the seep. Seep 4 had a conductivity of 90.3 uS/cm. Seep 5 had a conductivity of 23.6 uS/cm.No new violations noted. Violations still remain outstanding from Inspection Reports 3305227, 3306834, 3445592, and 3467217.

Comments: On March 19 2025 the Department conducted an inspection of the RWS Development 001 OG Well in regards to an incident reported to the Department of an explosion and fire at the well site on 3/19/2025 at 1:00 pm. Present during the inspection were several representatives from the Manor Volunteer Fire Department, Westmoreland City Fire Department, Jay Niehenke (Kriebel), Ronald Seich (Kriebel) Ben Dickun (Kriebel) and Charles Reaggle (DEP).-This is inspection 1 of a 2 part inspection-The findings are as follows:Upon the Department's arrival to the well site, no active fire was observed. The Department spoke to fire department representative Brian Williams who stated they used approximately 3200 gallons of municipal water from their firetruck as well as Dawn Dish Soap at a 0.6% per gallon concentration to extinguish the fire on site. While onsite, the SDS sheet for Dawn Dish Soap used was sent to the Department electronically by the Fire Department Representative Brian Williams. According to the SDS sheet, "Ecotoxicity- The product is not expected to be hazardous to the environment."Upon inspection of the production equipment, the Department observed damage to the equipment including a hole in the production tank as a result of the incident. Upon inspection of the hole in the production tank, the Department observed a small intermittent trickle of fluid from the production tank hole, down the side of the tank to the ground. A soil conductivity reading was taken directly under the hole in the tank with a reading of OR (over detectable range, >20.0 mS). The Department inquired what the most recent tank level was prior to the incident. Mr. Dickun stated that it was believed to be approximately 2 feet 6 inches from the bottom, however the date and exact measurement was unknown as that information is stored on a computer and was unable to be accessed at the time of the inspection. The Department took a measurement of the of the hole in the tank, which appeared level with the fluid level and obtained a measurement of approximately 2 feet 10.5 inches. While onsite, a truck arrived and began emptying the fluid from the production tank.The Department then assessed the well site to determine impacts resulting from any releases on the site as a result of the explosion/ fire and resulting measures taken to extinguish it. The Department observed a ditch/channel approximately 15 feet behind the well. The ditch appeared to run approximately 180 feet where it terminates just before a stream. The Department observed standing fluid in the ditch/channel in several locations. The Department also observed absorbent pads in the ditch that were reportedly placed placed by the Fire Department. Conductivity readings were taken of the fluid in the ditch in several locations with readings of OR, 6.28mS, 5.75mS, and 5.25mS. The conductivity readings appeared to decrease with distance from the well/production tank. No standing fluid was observed in the ditch in approximately the last 45 feet prior to terminating near the stream. There did not appear to be a recent flow path of fluid in the section of ditch from the last location of standing water to the remainder of ditch before the stream. Conductivity readings were taken in this area of the ditch with readings of 0.42mS, 0.34mS, and 0.42mS.The Department then took conductivity readings of the water in the stream. A conductivity reading was taken upstream of where the ditch appears to terminate with a reading of 0.65mS. There appeared to be a large amount of debris and trash in the stream and on the stream bank upstream where this conductivity reading was taken. A conductivity reading was then taken in the stream in the area where the ditch appears to terminate prior to the stream with a reading of 0.90mS. No sheen, discoloration, or foaming was observed in the stream.

Inspection Date: 5/02/2022
Comments: Responded to an oil spill at this gas well location. The plug for the heater tube in the stock tank failed and allowed oil to leak out of the tank and into the diking. With the recent heavy rains, it appears the fluid in the diking overflowed through an open freshwater drain pipe and an inadequate diking height in spots. There was a ditch located on the backside of the diking where some of the oil flowed into but most of the oil appears to have gone out the freshwater drain pipe and then down the lease road. The lease road was approximately 55 yards long and pockets of oil were located throughout it and then into the weeds heading towards that same ditch that runs parallel to the lease road. The ditch empties into the Lake Wilhelm Road ditch. This Lake Wilhelm Road ditch just had a sheen of oil of oil on it west of the driveway. The last spot oil was seen in this ditch was about 10 yards east of the driveway culvert pipe outfall. No oil or sheen was seen emptying into or in the main stream of Calvin Clark Run itself. The oil was mostly contained with sorbent pads and by the grass and brush in the ditch. Based on site observations, it appears that less than 1 bbl of oil was released outside the diking area. With the heavy rains predicted again in the next 2 days, it was suggested for them to install a siphon dam in the field ditch right before it enters into the road ditch. A small excavator arrived on site and was in the process of doing this when I left. They were getting a vac truck out there today to remove all the fluid in the tank to stop the leaking of the oil. At 3:31 PM, Matt Kleese from Diamond Energy called me. He reported that they had just removed around 50 bbls of old motor oil from that stock tank. He said this well produces very little fluid and it was definitely old oil (he thinks motor oil). So he feels somebody had apparently dumped old motor oil in this tank. He said that he is probably going to file a police report on this incident.

Comments: On May 15, 2025, an inspection was conducted at the Schimizzi S and M 1 well site in Hempfield Township, Westmoreland County. This inspection was conducted to follow up to IR 3944466, where violations were left outstanding due to no Act 9 sign and Emergency Response plan (ERP) onsite. Also, at the time of this inspection, no response of any kind has been received from the operator regarding violations issued in 3093059 or any subsequent cleanup that may have been conducted. At the time of IR 3484420, the soil conductivity onsite appeared to be comparable with that of the surrounding soil. At the time of IR 3944466, no staining or distressed vegetation was observed around the production tanks.The following was observed:No Act 9 sign is present at the well site entrance, and no ERP was found anywhere onsite (see photo 1). The production tanks appear to be sound at the time of inspection, with no evidence of fluids leaking to the ground around them. However, they still lack secondary containment, as is required at unconventional well sites (see photos 2-5). The top hatch of the production tank closest to the well head was not observed on the ground during this inspection. The Department recommended in IR 3944466 that this top hatch be replaced onto the production tank to prevent possible overflowing with rainwater.The well site overall exhibits greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation concerns are observed at this time (see photos 1 and 4). The access road remains stabilized with gravel. The well tag that was affixed to the well head during the time of IR 3944466 appears to have been removed. No staining or distressed vegetation was observed on the ground around the well head (see photo 6). The additional piping and production equipment that does not appear to be in use remains onsite (see photo 7). The Department recommends that equipment onsite that is not in use for production is removed from site. The well postings onsite include contact information for Dorso LP (see photos 8 and 9).Based on observations from this inspection, violations that were continued from IR 3944466 shall remain outstanding, as it appears that no corrective action has been taken onsite since the date of that inspection and no response of any kind to IR 3093059 has been received to date.

Comments: Onsite to investigate Complaint # 373782 dated 7/20/2023.There is an active discharge of fluid from the Tank Battery of the Lower Reno oil lease that is permitted and operated by Petro Erie Inc.. The public water supply for the town of Reno, PA is under a "Do Not Consume Advisory" based upon an increase in TDS for the Bellows Spring Cistern (owned and operated by Venango Water Company).The tank battery consists of (2) 210bbl steel tanks and (4) 100bbl poly tanks. The earthen dike appears to be lined with a plastic liner. There is a dike drain that is located in the southwest corner of the dike. The valve on the drain pipe is open and fluid is flowing to the ground. The area inside the dike appears to have been impacted by produced fluid from the tanks. A pipeline between two of the poly tanks was actively dripping fluid. Field screening inside the dike were conducted with the soil probe for conductivity, and all readings were above the range of the meter (20,000uS).The discharge from the dike drain flows south across an open area and into a wooded area. There is a visible impact area extending from the dike drain in an irregular pattern approximately 80 yards from the earthen dike and approximately ranging from 6' to 25' in width. Field screening within the impacted area was conducted approximately every 10 yards. Conductivity measurements ranged from 11,000uS to above the range of the meter (20,000uS). Several areas outside of the impacted area were checked with the soil probe and the levels ranged between 60uS to 164uS. An oil sheen is visible within the flowing water and dead vegetation is also observed including several large cherry trees within the impacted area. The amount of discharged fluid is unknown and based upon the observations onsite it appears that the discharge has been occurring for some time.The dike drain was closed by DEP staff at 8:45am to stop the continued discharge of fluid outside of the earthen dike.Water samples were collected at the dike drain outlet (discharge point) and sent to the lab for analysis. Water samples were also collected at the Bellows Spring Cistern (41.422360 -79.764490) which is a source for a public water supply of the town of Reno, PA.While onsite the Department talked with the operator/owner (Harry Rhoades) via a phone conversation. The discharge and the potential that the discharge may be impacting the public water supply was discussed with Mr. Rhoades. Mr. Rhoades insisted that he does not discharge his brine and that he could provide disposal documents. It was stated that the dike drain was left open because of forecasted rain. Violations are cited.The Oil and Gas Inspector (OGI) will be conducting a separate well compliance inspection for the well and other wells on the lease.

Comments: On October 30 2024, the Department conducted a follow up inspection of the Louis Yemc 1 Well in Hempfield Township, Westmoreland County.At the time of the inspection, the well was reported to be plugged (according to Department records) with no monument present. The access road appears to be unrestored. The Operator has provided the following information for the access road to remain:1. Map of area being proposing to remain including if there would PCSM proposed in that area.2. Map or overlay of how site was to be restored.3. Include property boundaries. With the information that was provided by the Operator, the Department has approved for the access road is to remain. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation issues were observed during this inspection. There appears to be no residual waste or plugging material left on the well site since the pad is no longer there. Equipment has been left onsite. The former site is nearing 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth with the exception of the recently dug pit for the removal of the pit contents. The recently dug pit was temporarily stabilized, at the time of this inspection. Filter sock has been placed at the downslope of the former recently dig pit as recommended by the Department. This filter sock was placed to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation issues.Plugging was completed on 12/08/2023 (according to Department records), therefore the site should have been restored no later than 9/8/2024. The well site restoration report shall be issued within 60 days after restoration of the well site in accordance with 78.65(3).Based on today's inspection, violations shall be closed for failure to have temporary E and S BMPs installed to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation issues. Failure to have the site restored shall remain outstanding.

Outstanding violations of 78.57(a), 91.34(a), and 78.54 are being issued.
